executive_summary: Northwind Labs is a young European AI routing vendor that is moving upmarket. Since late 2025 it has acquired a planning startup, raised a Series A, shipped a natural-language Copilot, and landed its largest enterprise deal. Hiring for US enterprise sales and a switch to usage-based pricing suggest an expansion push beyond Europe. Customer sentiment is strong on routing quality but shows friction in onboarding and reporting. Reports of the Series A size conflict ($15M vs $18M); the company's own press release is the more credible figure.

timeline.title: Acquires Routely
timeline.description: All-stock acquisition of a seven-person route-planning team, adding a multi-stop planning engine.

timeline.title: Announces Series A
timeline.description: Round led by Cobalt Ridge Ventures to expand to mid-market forwarders and double engineering.

timeline.title: Launches Northwind Copilot
timeline.description: Plain-English dispatcher assistant, directly challenging Parcelmind and Fleetwise; well received on Product Hunt.

timeline.title: Open-sources northwind-sdk 1.0
timeline.description: Apache 2.0 SDK with Python and TypeScript clients and a routing simulator.

timeline.title: Signs Harborline Freight
timeline.description: Multi-year deployment across 40 terminals, its largest enterprise contract so far.

timeline.title: Moves to usage-based pricing
timeline.description: Per-seat licences replaced by per-optimised-route billing; existing customers grandfathered until renewal.

timeline.title: Ships v3.2
timeline.description: Multi-carrier routing API, EU data-residency controls (beta) and voice input for Copilot.

strategy.statement: Moving upmarket from European mid-market forwarders to large enterprise networks.
Building a defensible AI layer by combining an acquired planning engine, Copilot, and an open SDK that seeds an ecosystem.
Aligning revenue with customer value through usage-based pricing (inferred; no revenue data available).
Likely preparing a US push: enterprise sales roles in Chicago and Atlanta alongside fresh funding (inference, not announced).

strengths.point: Strong routing accuracy reputation and a 4.6/5 review average.
Marquee enterprise reference in Harborline Freight.
Fast shipping cadence across API, SDK and Copilot.

weaknesses.point: Onboarding can take weeks and support replies are described as slow.
Limited legacy TMS integrations, raised at the Copilot launch.

opportunities.point: EU data residency, once generally available, could unlock switching demand.
Open SDK and multi-carrier API can attract partners and integrators.

threats.point: AI-first rival Parcelmind already ships a comparable assistant.
Incumbent Fleetwise competes on installed base.
Pricing change may create churn risk at renewal for per-seat customers.

competitors.name: Parcelmind
competitors.rationale: AI-first rival with a comparable assistant released a year earlier and stronger reporting per reviewers.

competitors.name: Fleetwise
competitors.rationale: Incumbent with installed base; reviewers say Northwind is more flexible to set up.

contradictions.resolution: Treat $15M as the working figure: it comes from the company's own dated release (primary source), while the $18M profile is a secondary aggregator two days later. A later extension cannot be ruled out.

contradictions.topic: Customer experience: high ratings vs slow onboarding
contradictions.resolution: Not strictly incompatible, but one anecdote cannot be weighed against 87 reviews. Needs more onboarding data.

gaps: No verified revenue, customer count or churn data.
Harborline contract value and terms are not disclosed.
No independent confirmation of the planned US expansion.

findings.claim: A company-profile database lists Northwind's February 2026 Series A at $18M.
findings.snippet: closed an $18 million Series A in February 2026

findings.claim: Northwind has 14 open roles: 9 in ML/platform engineering, 3 in enterprise sales (two of them in Chicago and Atlanta) and 2 in customer success.
findings.snippet: nine in machine learning and platform engineering, three in enterprise sales, and two in customer success. Two of the sales roles are based in Chicago and Atlanta

findings.claim: Northwind was founded in 2023 by Maya Okafor and Daan Visser and currently serves European freight forwarders.
findings.snippet: was founded in 2023 by Maya Okafor and Daan Visser

findings.claim: From 14 July 2026 Northwind switched from per-seat licences to usage-based pricing billed per optimised route.
findings.snippet: moves from per-seat licences to usage-based pricing, billed per optimised route

findings.claim: Northwind announced a $15M Series A led by Cobalt Ridge Ventures in February 2026, earmarked for mid-market expansion and doubling engineering.
